A threshold line inside a track

Source: R/geom-track-hline.R
geom_track_hline.Rd

geom_hline() draws at yintercept on the angle axis, because a track's y is an angle (spec sec.4.2). For a threshold in the band's own units use this instead: value goes through the same normalisation the track's values went through, so the line and the data always share one scale.

Usage

geom_track_hline(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  stat = "identity",
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  band = NULL,
  value,
  linetype = "dashed",
  linewidth = 0.4,
  colour = "grey30",
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = FALSE
)

Arguments

mapping, data, stat, position, na.rm, show.legend, inherit.aes

Standard ggplot2::layer() arguments. data is optional; the nodes come from the plot's layout.

...

Passed to ggplot2::layer(), for further line settings.

band

The track to draw in: a declared band name, or c(r0, r1). Defaults to the band of a track layer already on the plot.

value

Threshold in the track's value units, not radii. A vector draws several lines.

linetype, linewidth, colour

Appearance of the line.

Value

A ggplot2 layer.

Details

The line is drawn per node – one arc inside each node's own span – so it reads as "this node's threshold" rather than a ring passing through the gaps.

See also

geom_track(), geom_track_axis()

Examples

links <- data.frame(from = c("a", "b"), to = c("b", "c"))
ggcircos(links, tracks = c(v = 0.2)) +
  geom_track(data = data.frame(id = c("a", "b", "c"), v = c(0.2, 0.5, 0.8)),
             aes(x = v), node = id, band = "v") +
  geom_track_hline(band = "v", value = 0.5)
